en: Vimānavatthu: The Mansion of the Man,
Chapter on the Great Chariot (Mahārathavagga)
11. The Second Nāga-Vimāna Story “Having mounted a great nāga,
a supreme elephant entirely white;”
Surrounded by a host of women, you wandered from forest to forest,
illuminating all directions.
The stars are like medicinal herbs.
By what means is your complexion such as this?
…pe…
"And your complexion shines in all directions.
Thus was that son of the gods,
being questioned by Vaṅgīsa, filled with joy.
When asked a question,
he explained it as the fruit of that very action:
"When I was among humans, having become a human..."
I was a lay follower of the One with Vision;
I abstained from taking life and avoided what is not given in the world.
I did not drink intoxicants, nor did I speak falsehood;
I was content with my own wife;
and with a confident heart, [I gave] food and drink.
I gave extensive gifts with due care.
Because of that, such is my complexion... [and so on].
"And my radiance shines in all directions.
Thus ends the twelfth Nāga-vimāna, the eleventh [in this section].
